subject: english
question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

He said, "How long have you been waiting?"

options.text: He asked how long had I been waiting.
He said how long I was waiting.
He asked how long I have been waiting.
He asked how long I had been waiting.

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. He asked how long I had been waiting .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and is a question in the present perfect tense: *"How long have you been waiting?"*
 
• When converting to indirect speech:
 
 
• The reporting verb changes to **asked** as it is a question.
 
• The tense of the direct speech changes from **present perfect** (*have been*) to **past perfect** (*had been*).
 
• The pronoun **"you"** changes to **"I"** to match the subject in indirect speech.
 
 

Correct sentence: *He asked how long I had been waiting*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for changing tense in indirect speech:**
 
 
• Present perfect tense (*have/has + past participle*) changes to past perfect tense (*had + past participle*).
 
• Present tense verbs change to past tense verbs.
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Direct speech: He said, "I have finished my homework."
 
• Indirect speech: He said that he had finished his homework.
